title: The $35 swoosh
hook: Nike's swoosh was drawn by a student who was paid $35 for it.
peek: In 1971 a graphic design student named Carolyn Davidson drew a simple tick-like mark for a small running-shoe company. She billed $35. The company became Nike, and years later it thanked her with a gold ring and shares.
lede: In 1971 Carolyn Davidson was a graphic design student at Portland State University, where Phil Knight taught accounting. Knight's small shoe company needed a mark for the side of its new shoes, and he paid her $2 an hour to come up with one. After about 17 hours of work she billed $35, and the design she delivered became the Nike swoosh.

bullets.text: Knight was not thrilled. He is reported to have said he did not love it but that it might grow on him. With a deadline for the new shoes, the company went with it.
The company was named after Nike, the Greek goddess of victory. The swoosh is often read as a wing, or as a sign of movement and speed.
The mark appeared on Nike's first own-brand shoes in 1972. Davidson kept doing design work for the company for several years as it grew.
In 1983 Knight invited Davidson to a meeting and gave her a gold ring in the shape of the swoosh, set with a small diamond, along with an envelope of Nike shares.
